cases.description: Two IPv4 feeds in one Deny group, an IPv6 Deny group and a DNSBL group: the first manual Update builds every set and the DNSBL data; a retry Update naming every feed finds each unchanged (the mock answers 304 to the ETag it gave); a retry Update naming one IPv4 feed after its body changed rebuilds that group only.
A Deny group of two IPv4 feeds, one whose URL answers 404: the failed feed gets no success outcome and the group is built from the feed that downloaded.

An IPv4 group and a DNSBL group, both built once; then both bodies change and a manual Update of scope ip with force download runs: the IPv4 set is rebuilt from the new body, the DNSBL data stays as the first Update left it.
cases.ordering: a narrower scope leaving other work pending

cases.description: An IPv4 group and a DNSBL group built once; the bodies then change on the server and a manual Update with force parse runs: the sets are rebuilt from the downloads already on disk, so they keep the first bodies.
An IPv4 group built once; its body then changes on the server and an apply Update runs: no feed is checked or downloaded, no outcome is reported, and the set stays as it was.
A DNSBL feed that lists IP addresses beside domains, with DNSBL IP on (Deny_Both): the DNSBL stage collects the addresses and the IP stage publishes them as pfB_DNSBLIP_v4 and _v6.
cases.ordering: DNSBLIP built after the DNSBL stage and consumed by the IP stage

cases.description: A Permit IPv4 group, and a Deny IPv4 group whose only feed holds comments only: the permit set holds its members; the empty set is today's placeholder, which Core leaves out (owner question 1).
